course: The strongest aspect of the course is that it is a deeper understanding of methodology that is required for anyone who plans an academic career in the future. The weakest part of the course is possibly that it shouldn't need to be a course. Although the student certainly learns something new in the class, most of the important lessons of methodology are things a Masters student already knows or should know at this point (considering there is a prep year in History as well). This is not a personal attack to the delivery of the lectures or the professor but a note on the contents of a class so oriented to teaching methodology.

This course is a must for all historians in terms of providing them with the basic methodological knowledge and illustrating what can and cannot included into the research. However in my opinion this course lacks the initial theoretical background and the ontological descriptions. It might be better to put an emphasize on the research methods aspect of this course.
